🚀 Databricks just made “𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲-𝘃𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗲𝗱 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀” (TVFs) as easy as any other DataFrame call.

Previously, if we wanted to use a TVF like 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗹𝗼𝗱𝗲 or a custom UDTF, we often had to register a temporary view and then use 𝘀𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗸.𝘀𝗾𝗹() to write a SQL query. This worked, but it could make our Python code feel a bit clunky and less "DataFrame-native."

The new API, available from DBR 16.1, lets us call these functions directly on our DataFrames. This means:
 • 𝗖𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗻𝗲𝗿 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗲: Keep your logic entirely within the DataFrame API, making it easier to read and maintain.
 • 𝗕𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆: Chain TVF calls with other DataFrame transformations like .filter() and .select() seamlessly.
 • 𝗣𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿𝗳𝘂𝗹 𝗥𝗼𝘄-𝗹𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀: With lateral joins (in DBR 17.0+), you can apply a TVF to each row of your DataFrame, which is amazing for tasks like generating series or expanding nested data.

📖 𝗗𝗲𝗲𝗽-𝗱𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗯𝗹𝗼𝗴: https://lnkd.in/dw_iVF8V

𝗟𝗲𝘁'𝘀 𝘀𝗲𝗲 𝗶𝘁 𝗶𝗻 𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻!
Imagine we have a dataset of online orders, where each order contains a list of products. Our goal is to create a new row for each product in each order.

𝗦𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗸 𝗦𝗤𝗟 𝘃𝘀 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗙𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗲𝗔𝗣𝗜 𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗮𝗰𝗵 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗹𝗼𝗱𝗲:
